subject: Clarify indemnity trigger & damages scope for IP infringement carve-out
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helixtx.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@helixtx.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments - indemnity / IP carve-outs

Connor —

Thanks for sending the MSA. Our legal team flagged the indemnity / liability section. High level: Helix needs an explicit carve-out to the liability cap for direct damages stemming from third-party IP infringement claims attributable to Redwood’s delivery of the Service. We understand you have a standard cap, but for IP we need unrestricted recovery or, at minimum, a separate reasonable (but uncapped) remedy tied to actual infringement damages.

Couple quick asks so we can move this internally:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an IP indemnity that survives termination and is not subject to the order-form monetary cap?
- If Redwood cannot accept fully uncapped exposure, will you consider a defined escrow or insurance-backed remedy (we can share limits) and a carve-out for equitable injunctive relief?

Attached our redlines for the MSA (see callout on §9.b). Happy to jump on a call this week — we’re targeting an internal approval by Friday.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Contracts, Helix Therapeutics
laura.chen@helixtx.com
Attachments: Redline_MSA_Helix_v3.docx

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helixtx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments - indemnity / IP carve-outs

Laura — appreciate the quick read. Looping in Karthik from Legal and Grace (AM lead) to coordinate. High level from Sales: we want to keep predictable unit economics for the deal but also be reasonable on IP claims that are clearly Redwood-origin.

Karthik, Grace — Helix is asking for IP indemnity outside the order form cap (or an alternative of escrow / insurance + injunctive carve-out). They have an internal sign-off target of Friday. Can Legal propose specific language we can send back today? Also flag any material commercial/price impacts we should raise with pricing.

Next steps I propose: Karthik to propose redline language limited to (i) third-party patent/copyright/DSA claims caused by Redwood’s model/service, (ii) remediation/defense obligations, (iii) damages either uncapped or subject to an alternate remedy (insurance/escrow), plus a narrow survival clause. If we can get a defend-and-indemnify template with an escrow fallback, I can propose it in the commercial thread.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Laura Chen <laura.chen@helixtx.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MSA comments - indemnity / IP carve-outs

Laura / Connor —

Thanks — I reviewed Helix's redlines and here are two alternate positions we can put on the table today. Draft language is pasted below; I will attach a tracked-redline version to the MSA. Please advise which (if any) Helix prefers so we can close the loop.

Option A (Preferred for Redwood - limited carve-out):
"Notwithstanding the limitation of liability in Section X, Redwood shall indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging that Redwood's Service, as delivered to Customer under this Agreement, infringes a third party's intellectual property rights, provided that Customer (i) notifies Redwood promptly upon becoming aware of such claim, (ii) allows Redwood to control the defense and settlement of the claim, and (iii) mitigates its damages. Liability under this indemnity shall be subject to the Order Form monetary cap except that Redwood's obligation to pay amounts awarded by a court for direct damages resulting from an adjudicated finding of willful infringement shall be uncapped."

Rationale: preserves overall cap but removes cap for narrow set of judicially-determined willful infringement damages.

Option B (Conservative compromise - insured/escrow hybrid):
"Notwithstanding the limitation of liability in Section X, Redwood shall (i) procure and maintain commercially reasonable intellectual property insurance covering third-party IP claims with limits of not less than $5,000,000 during the term of this Agreement and (ii) be liable for direct damages awarded by a final adjudication to the extent not covered by such insurance, up to a separate IP indemnity cap equal to $5,000,000. Injunctive relief shall remain available to Customer without regard to the foregoing cap."

Rationale: caps Redwood's residual exposure while guaranteeing a funded remedy; aligns to our insurance posture.

Technical/legal notes: the trigger for indemnity should require Redwood to have made a material contribution (e.g., the infringing portion originates from Redwood's proprietary components or model customization for Helix). We should avoid an open-ended indemnity for third-party content that the Customer uploads without indemnity.

I will attach a tracked-change MSA with Option A as primary and Option B as fallback. If Helix prefers a different insurance limit, flag now. Connor — if this moves forward materially it will impact price vs standard terms; provide me with the ACV and any ask on credits/commitments so I can model risk tolerance.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helixtx.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments - indemnity / IP carve-outs

Karthik —

Appreciate the thoughtful options. Helix legal is unlikely to accept Option A as currently drafted because (1) requiring a judicial finding of willful infringement as the only uncapped remedy is a high bar, and (2) the carveout language still leaves open exposure for large actual damages that won't be covered by insurance.

We'd like to propose a middle ground: Redwood will (i) maintain IP insurance with a minimum limit of $10M, (ii) accept an uncapped obligation for equitable relief (injunctive relief) and for direct damages to the extent a court finds infringement, and (iii) for settlements, Redwood will either fund an escrow equal to the settlement amount above insurance limits or accept liability up to a mutual cap of $15M (whichever is lower). This structure gives Helix contractual comfort for settlements without requiring litigation to a final judgment.

We can accept a narrow carve-out that excludes Customer-provided content and third-party model artifacts; the trigger should be limited to Redwood-origin code/model/service components.

Laura

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helixtx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA comments - indemnity / IP carve-outs

Laura — thanks for the counter. I think there is a realistic path to agreement. Proposed commercial path: Redwood can agree to the insured/escrow hybrid if Helix will accept the following phone-home items: (a) minimum IP insurance limit of $7.5M (Redwood can provide certificate of insurance); (b) settlement handling: Redwood controls defense but will not unreasonably withhold consent to settlements that bind Helix; (c) mutual cap on settlements above insurance of $10M, with an escrow option if Helix prefers to fund bilateral escrow for any settlement between $5M and $10M.

We will need an internal pricing uplift to cover additional insurance/escrow exposure; I will share the proposed uplift and revised order-form by EOD tomorrow. Karthik — can you prepare the tracked MSA with Helix's proposed settlement flow and our hybrid numbers so Laura can take this to her GC?

If Helix is OK with the $7.5M / $10M structure we can lock the commercial terms and proceed to signature.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: IP_Claims_Process_Summary.pdf
